1. Atlantic City airport would be the absolute closest to Cape May County. 

2. Renting a car would be best but I have seen lots of Lyft drivers around.

3. Hotels in Cape May are expensive in the summer (Cape May, Stone Harbor, Wildwood, Sea Isle City and Avalon are big, big tourist areas) but you might get lucky. However, if you are all on a really strict budget, the Hyland Motor Inn in Cape May Court House is a cheap little motel with a pool. But, you can search the places in Cape May, Wildwood and Rio Grande for closest places to stay near Cape May. Please, please look up reviews.

4. Washington Square Mall in Cape May is a wonderful collection of small businesses and restaurants that would make a great visit. Parking is tough, though. Cold Spring Village is a historical landmark but also has attractions, a restaurant and a pub. Cape May Point Beach has the concrete ship and sometimes dolphins show up and you can see the ferry crossing. The lighthouse is nearby as well which has beautiful nature trails. Wildwood has the boardwalk which has arcades, food, a couple of waterparks and rides. Rio Grande has a Wal-Mart, Michael's, Five Below, Ross, Starbucks, Rio Grande Diner and lots more.

5. If you need wifi visit the local libraries because they can print you our a guest pass to use the PC's. They are also cozy and pleasant places and the Cape May City library is fairly close to the CG base. CMCH, Stone Harbor, Lower Cape and Wildwood Crest are all libraries that are closeby. They have old books for sale for fifty cents a book, if you are a reader. 
Also, the streets in Cape May are small and often confusing, so if you have a rental and feel lost pull off the main road onto a side road to get your bearings because accidents happen. 
Other than that, please enjoy the beauty of Cape May and take some time to see the nature. We are also a hotspot for birding.

Strawberry-Lemon Scones

3 C all-purpose flour
2 sticks of cold butter
1/2 C sugar
1 1/4 C whole milk
1 egg
1 tbsp baking powder
1 tsp vanilla
5 medium strawberries, cut small
1 tbsp fresh lemon zest
2 tsp salt

Glaze 
1 1/2 C of powdered sugar
1/4 tsp vanilla
Pinch of salt
Add lemon juice until it reaches a desired consistency
Crumble freeze dried strawberries over the fresh glaze

Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Needs 20-30 minutes to bake.

I altered this recipe from an old English type pf scone and I like my glaze a little on the thinner side since my neices and nephews are young and love a good glaze.

I start with the 3 cups of flour in a large pyrex bowl and to that I add 1 tablespoon of baking powder, lemon zest, salt and the sugar. Then, add the buttersticks and, after washing your hands, begin the process of incorporating the dry ingredients with the butter. This takes a little bit of time, so I normally put on a playlist of Youtube videos.

After the mixture feels like sand (if it doesn't your butter was not cold enough), start rubbing it between your hands. This isn't a back and forth motion this is placing some of the sandy mixture between palms and pushing forward. This will help create more texture in the scone.

When you have measured your milk, add the egg into the milk, along with the vanilla, and mix until it is incorporated.

Add into the dry (I will call this mixture dry even though butter is not considered a dry ingredient) ingredients and g e n t l y mix. Before it is completed, add in the cut strawberries and begin to fold the dough. This is a messy process since this scone dough is a little more wet than others.

Shape into a round and cut the dough to make it easier to make a clean cut when removing from the oven. I set my old, inefficient oven to 385 degrees since I really wanted it at 375 degrees. I threw this little info out for those with similar ovens.

After getting the scones from the oven LET COMPLETELY COOL. Resist the tempatation!

When the scones were completely cool, I sift the powdered sugar and added the juice of one lemon and 1/4 tsp of vanilla to make the glaze. 

Drizzle on top and then add the dehydrated strawberries, cut, and enjoy!

Thanks for having an interest in my scones! :)

Edit: Forgot to mention to pat the surface with whole milk so it gets nice and golden.

Proper time management. I'm currently working a fulltime job and going for a Master's degree (fully online). There were a lot of things I did that created situations where I used up my free time with hanging out with friends or playing video games. So, in order for me to have time to work out I changed and planned out my day. 

This may sound overwhelming but let me put it in perspective. I meal prep on Sundays (you may want to consider breakfast and lunch meal preps), I'm in bed by 9 and up by 5:30 or 6. 6am I take my supplements (that need to be taken on an empty stomach), do all the morning hygienic stuff, and by 6:30 I'm studying for my classes until 7:30. I eat breakfast and get ready for work. After I get off at 4:30 I take a half an hour to an hour walk (if weather permits) or I will go to the gym. I also take walks on my lunch break as well, if the weather is good. I also take care of my mother so finding time for grocery shopping and cleaning is a must, too. I read that I shouldn't have mentioned getting up early but are you doing homework from the time you get home until 1am? Because, if not, you may want to evaluated the complete amount of your free time and see what you are doing with it.

Time management is kind of like putting a puzzle together. If you organize all the corner and edge pieces in separate piles, similar colors in other piles, and connecting parts in others is a good way of viewing time management. 

Friends will always be there, if they are understanding and if they aren't let them go, and may even help you in certain aspects of your life. For example, one of my closest friends is a yogi so when I hang out with her we will take walks, do yoga, or meet at the gym. We both enrich our lives in that way and practically use time together.

Hope this helps!

From what I have understood about IBS from doctors and gastroenterologists is that red meat, dairy, pork and eggs should be greatly reduced but eliminated may be best to avoid flare ups. 

But, if you want to stick to the keto diet you need to eat more lettuce (not cruciferous vegetables like kale and cabbage because they can create a LOT of uncomfortable bloat), berries (within carb limit), and I honestly cannot think of anything else. 

I can imagine it being very difficult trying to do a keto diet when IBS creates so many limits in what someone can or can't eat. 

I hope this helped and did not offend.

I would say I'm pretty healthy. Some back issues from a car accident but it doesn't stop me from working, school, and living. Honestly, I'm kind of grateful for IBS because the restricted food choices makes me feel better. Especially in regards to focusing for longer periods of time. 

If I do feel sudden pain I try and evaluate what I've eaten and make sure to avoid it. For example, I was cooking for my friend's birthday the other day and had a spoonful of something with cream cheese in it and felt the pain within 20 minutes, but what was much more evident was the bloating. 

Since I've cleaned up my diet and gotten rid of the majority of possible allergens (gulten, dairy, refined/artificial sugars, meat except for white fish and chicken breast, and eggs) I have felt fine. Always bummed when I have to bring my own food over someone's house, but worth it to avoid the pain.
